clue.text: Americans mad about work, as this lot are

definitions.note: The definition is a pointer rather than a synonym: 'this lot' means the people the first half of the clue has just described, so the sentence defines and builds at the same time.

indicators.note: Someone mad has lost their right mind, and letters that have lost theirs will not stay in the order the clue set them.
To be mad about something is to be wrapped up in it, and the wrapping is literal here: the shuffled letters close round the piece that follows.

parts.note: nine letters of raw material, not a nationality
a machine with plenty of go is one that works, and the pair sits inside the shuffle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Americans' looks like the subject of the sentence and is really the fodder. The closing words point back at the people the clue has just described, which is where the definition hides.
explanation.definitionFit: as this lot are -> ERGOMANIACS: 'this lot' points back at the people the clue has described, and an ergomaniac is someone obsessively driven to work.

clue.text: Those who lure models in secret

indicators.note: To model clay is to work it into a new shape, and the letters beside the word are worked into a new order the same way.

parts.note: eight letters of fodder, taken exactly as the clue writes them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has glamorous models luring somebody quietly. The instruction is that same word as a verb, the shaping kind rather than the catwalk kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who lure -> ENTICERS: an enticer is one who tempts somebody in, and the plural agent noun answers 'those who' exactly.

clue.text: Mixture of lust and rage expressed in body movements

indicators.note: A mixture is what you get when things are stirred together, and nothing in one ends up where it started.

parts.note: the two nouns supply all eight letters between them

explanation.walkthrough: Desire and anger read as a state of mind in the surface. The answer is about how feelings show instead: hands, shoulders and face rather than words.
explanation.definitionFit: expressed in body movements -> GESTURAL: gestural is the adjective for anything conveyed by gesture, so it covers meaning carried by the body rather than speech.

clue.text: She has the Man in the Moon's darkish features

definitions.meaning: a very common woman's given name, the Latin and Italian form of Mary

definitions.text: the Man in the Moon's darkish features
definitions.meaning: the dark patches that make up the face on the Moon are flat lava plains

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses meet in five letters. The astronomical one is a plural: each dark plain is a mare, Latin for sea, because early observers took them for water.
explanation.definitionFit: She -> MARIA is a woman's name; the Man in the Moon's darkish features -> MARIA, the dark lava plains that early astronomers mistook for seas.

clue.text: Old lady's man on board in Chinese port

parts.note: nan is the familiar British word for a grandmother
the board is a chessboard, and the man on it that the whole game turns on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' wants to be a sailor and is a chess piece. The city is spelt Nanjing today; crosswords still like the older transliteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese port -> NANKING: Nanking is the older English spelling of Nanjing, the city and river port on the Yangtze, so the definition names it plainly.

clue.text: Song cycles "about" a mountain? On the contrary, it's "in"

indicators.note: about means going around something, here the containing letters
on the contrary flips the containment: the mountain goes about the song, not the song about the mountain

parts.note: taken as written
MT is the standard abbreviation for mount or mountain

indicators.note: cycles means the first letter rides round to the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about putting a song cycle around a mountain, which the setter then turns on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words are a set of instructions that 'On the contrary' overturns: the mountain wraps round the cycled song rather than the other way, and the result means 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means in the middle of or surrounded by, so it can replace 'in' in a phrase like 'in the crowd'.

clue.text: Son starts drinking and painting in dotty fashion

indicators.note: A word's start is its opening letter, so the name before it gives up one character and no more.

parts.note: the opening letter of Son
to tipple is to drink, steadily and habitually

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' is doing two jobs at once: it keeps the surface silly, and it names the technique precisely, since the paint really does go on as separate dots.
explanation.definitionFit: painting in dotty fashion -> STIPPLING: stippling builds an image out of small dots rather than strokes, so the phrase describes the method exactly.

clue.text: No shame occasionally offering some resistance

indicators.note: What happens occasionally happens every so often rather than every time, so the letters are picked at every other step.

parts.note: every second letter of the two words, counting from the second

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a shameless heckler standing his ground. 'Some' is the quiet signal that the definition wants a measure rather than an act of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: some resistance -> OHM: the ohm is the unit in which electrical resistance is measured, so the phrase asks for a quantity of it.

clue.text: Round lump sum of money in ancient Greece

definitions.text: sum of money in ancient Greece

parts.note: a round shape drawn on the page is the letter O
a bolus is a soft rounded lump, of chewed food or of medicine

explanation.walkthrough: Worth banking: crosswords are fond of ancient money, and this coin was one sixth of a drachma, the fare traditionally left for the ferryman.
explanation.definitionFit: sum of money in ancient Greece -> OBOLUS: an obolus was a small-value coin of the classical Greek world, so the phrase names a piece of that currency.

clue.text: Well I never pay for rubbish!

parts.note: 'My!' on its own is the same little cry of astonishment
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence it is a shopper refusing to be overcharged. Read as a clue it is three exclamations in a row, two of them building the third.
explanation.definitionFit: rubbish! -> MY FOOT: both are dismissive interjections meaning nonsense, flung at a statement the speaker declines to believe.

clue.text: A weapon was tested again after backfiring

indicators.note: A backfire sends the charge the wrong way down the barrel, so the letters run from the far end back to the start.

parts.note: to resit an exam is to take it again, and the clue wants the past tense

explanation.walkthrough: The exam sense of 'was tested again' is the way in, while the surface keeps you on a firing range watching a prototype being trialled.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon -> TASER: a taser is a hand-held stun gun that fires darts on wires, so the definition names it by its class.

clue.text: Follow one complaint about controversial feminist author

indicators.note: About here means turned right round, the way a ship goes about, so the assembled letters are read from their far end.

parts.note: what flows from an action follows from it, which is the sense being leaned on
the Roman numeral for one
a moan is a grumble or complaint

explanation.walkthrough: The equation of following with flowing is the setter's stretch, and it is the only step here that is not straight synonym work; everything else turns on reading the assembly backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: controversial feminist author -> NAOMI WOLF: she wrote The Beauty Myth, and her later claims about health and history are what earn 'controversial'.

clue.text: American bill to stop college group campaigning

indicators.note: To stop a gap is to plug it, so the letters named first are pushed into the middle of the ones named after.

parts.note: C is the standing abbreviation for college
a ring is a group acting together, usually with something to hide
US for the United States, the usual shorthand for American
a bill posted on a wall is an advertisement

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a legislature clamping down on student protest, so 'bill' looks like the parliamentary kind. It is the sort you paste up, and 'stop' is what you do to a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: campaigning -> CRUSADING: to crusade is to campaign hard for a cause, a figurative sense long detached from the medieval wars it comes from.

clue.text: What was foreshadowed by Percival Lowell initially before bowing out?

definitions.text: What was foreshadowed by Percival Lowell initially before bowing out?

indicators.note: before places the initials ahead of the rest
initially takes the first letter of each of the two names

parts.note: first letters of Percival and Lowell

indicators.note: bowing means bending out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle about what the American astronomer Percival Lowell predicted before he died.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowell predicted a ninth planet but died in 1916, 'bowing out' before it was found in 1930 at his observatory, so the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the planet discovered at Lowell Observatory after Lowell's search for a predicted 'Planet X'.

clue.text: Reckless driver runs over lad, out of his head when approaching corner

indicators.note: approaching puts the last piece right after the others

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: his head is the lad's first letter, and out of means it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to corner a market is to hog it, keeping it all to oneself

explanation.surface: A dangerous motorist mows down a boy who was out of his mind as he neared a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of his head' sounds like a drugged or crazy lad, but it means removing the lad's first letter, leaving AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a motorist who drives carelessly or selfishly, taking up more than a fair share of the road.

clue.text: German scorer in game has hard time making a comeback

parts.note: a hind is a female red deer, and deer are game

indicators.note: Something making a comeback returns along the way it went, so the letters just assembled are read from the end backwards.

parts.note: H is the grading stamped on a hard pencil
taken as it stands, ready to be turned round with the letter before it

explanation.walkthrough: 'German scorer' wants to be a footballer and 'in game' plays along with that. The scorer is a composer, and the game is the four-legged kind.
explanation.definitionFit: German scorer -> HINDEMITH: Paul Hindemith was a German composer, and a composer writes scores, which is the crossword's regular sideways word for one.

clue.text: Heads off to Ramallah in Palestine for vacation?

indicators.note: Heads are opening letters, and taking them off the words that follow is what leaves the four wanted here.

parts.note: each of the four words surrenders the letter it begins with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' reads as somebody setting out, which is the whole trick of the surface: it is really the instruction telling you to collect initials.
explanation.definitionFit: vacation -> TRIP: the question mark admits the stretch, since a trip is a short journey and taking one is the usual shape a vacation comes in.

clue.text: That place in east Alabama is heavenly

indicators.note: A thing said to be in another sits inside it, so these letters go between the two pieces named on either side.

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
AL is the US postal abbreviation for Alabama
the everyday word for a place already pointed at

explanation.walkthrough: The surface plants you in the American South, where the state is worth only two letters. The definition is the airy, unearthly sense, not praise for the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: heavenly -> ETHEREAL: ethereal means light and unearthly, belonging to the upper air, so 'heavenly' is being used in its otherworldly sense.

clue.text: The curse of Bibiana the Martyr

indicators.note: Here 'of' carries the sense of taken out of, and what is taken lies in one unbroken run in the words after it.

parts.note: the letters run consecutively across the join between the saint's name and her title

explanation.walkthrough: Saint Bibiana was an early Roman martyr, and she is here only because her name and title happen to run together the right way.
explanation.definitionFit: The curse -> ANATHEMA: an anathema is the Church's formal curse of excommunication, and in general use anything or anyone thoroughly detested.

clue.text: Odd parts declined by John Wayne? He pulled out at the last minute

definitions.text: He pulled out at the last minute

indicators.note: To decline something is to turn it down, so the letters in the odd positions are refused and the rest are kept.

parts.note: read the two names as one run and keep the letters in even positions

explanation.walkthrough: The film star is there for the surface, a leading man turning down a part, and for his letters. The definition is the Genesis story told with a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: He pulled out at the last minute -> ONAN: in Genesis, Onan spilled his seed on the ground rather than father a child for his brother's widow.

clue.text: Moonie's bum is foul-smelling

indicators.note: In the slang sense it means duff or faulty, and a faulty spelling is one whose letters have got out of place.

parts.note: seven letters of fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.walkthrough: A Moonie is a follower of the Unification Church, founded by Sun Myung Moon. The surface is rude about the sect; the setter only wants the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: foul-smelling -> NOISOME: noisome means offensive to the nose, nothing to do with noise, and it survives mainly in descriptions of smells.

clue.text: Announcement of giant squeeze

indicators.note: An announcement is made out loud, so what counts is the way the next word sounds rather than the way it is spelt.

parts.note: a titan is a giant, after the elder gods of Greek myth, and said aloud it is one letter away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' is the verb, not the noun: you tighten a grip rather than give one. The surface, meanwhile, is a bear hug from somebody enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: squeeze -> TIGHTEN: to tighten a strap or a grip is to squeeze it closer, the verb sense of making something less slack.

clue.text: I'm grateful for that piebald hack

parts.note: ta is the everyday British word for thanks
a pinto is a horse marked in patches of white and one other colour

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a scruffy horse, and a hack is a riding horse too, which is the trap. The definition is the computing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: hack -> TAP INTO: to hack a system is to tap into it, getting at data you have no right to, so both are verbs of unauthorised access.

clue.text: Change in pieces?

indicators.note: Something in pieces has been broken up, and letters broken up like that are put back in a different order.

parts.note: the six letters that get rearranged, doing double duty as the instruction

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the wink. Coined money really is change in pieces, so the clue describes its own answer while telling you what to do to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Change -> SPECIE: specie is coined money as opposed to paper, which is exactly what 'change' means when you ask to be given some.

clue.text: Backside of prominent Liberal observed in mature threesome

indicators.note: A thing's backside is its rear, so only the final letter of the word that follows is wanted.

parts.note: the last letter of prominent

indicators.note: What is observed in something has been spotted inside it, which is where this single letter has to go.

parts.note: fruit that has matured is ripe
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.walkthrough: Wiglaf's surface reads as gossip about a politician being watched. Underneath, 'mature' is the fruit sense and the Liberal is reduced to a party initial.
explanation.definitionFit: threesome -> TRIPLE: as a noun a triple is a group of three of anything, the same count that a threesome names.

clue.text: Pressure applied to city of old Georgia to eliminate dissidents?

parts.note: P is the scientist's symbol for pressure
Ur was a great city of ancient Sumer, in what is now southern Iraq
GE is the international code for the country of Georgia

explanation.walkthrough: Two Georgias are in play and the clue wants the Caucasus one, not the American state. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: to eliminate dissidents -> PURGE: to purge is to rid a party or a country of unwanted members, and a political clear-out is one instance of that.

clue.text: Tense setter is cutting short cigar

parts.note: the setter says 'I am', shortened to I'm

indicators.note: cutting short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a perfecto is a cigar thick in the middle and tapered at both ends

explanation.surface: A nervous setter is trimming a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for the nervous setter, but it is the grammatical tense. 'cutting short' drops the final O of PERFECTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is a verb tense for continuing or repeated past action, as in 'I was walking'.

clue.text: Old director general punches where it hurts

indicators.note: A punch lands inside whatever it hits, and inside the words that follow is where the letters wanted are sitting.

parts.note: the letters run on unbroken through the middle of the phrase, across two word breaks

explanation.walkthrough: John Reith was the BBC's first Director-General, and his name still labels high-minded broadcasting: the annual Reith Lectures are his memorial. The surface is a boxing report.
explanation.definitionFit: Old director general -> REITH: Lord Reith ran the BBC from its beginnings in the 1920s, and 'old' marks him out as a former holder of the post.

clue.text: Island to the west of my new house

indicators.note: West is left on a map and left along an across row, so the piece named first sits at the front.

parts.note: Capri is the island in the Bay of Naples
'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise doing the same job as 'My!'
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.walkthrough: Two small words carry the clue: 'house' is the astrological term, and 'my' is an exclamation rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: house -> CAPRICORN: the twelve signs of the zodiac are commonly called houses, so the definition names one of them by its category.

clue.text: Descartes declaring himself the personification of peace

parts.note: the philosopher's famous declaration starts from the first person, one letter long
his forename was Rene, spelt with an acute accent the grid cannot hold

explanation.walkthrough: Cogito ergo sum, I think therefore I am, is the declaration being pointed at, and the forename supplies the rest of a Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: the personification of peace -> IRENE: in Greek myth Irene is the goddess who embodies peace, so the definition points at a named divinity rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Scrumper evicting companion finally from flat

indicators.note: evicting means throwing out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: flat means level or even

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: last letter of companion

explanation.surface: An apple thief is thrown out of an apartment, ending a friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrumper steals apples from orchards, a British word; Eve took the apple in Eden. 'evicting companion finally' takes N out of EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve took fruit from the forbidden tree in Genesis, making her the first apple thief, a playful example.

clue.text: Henry recollected Ophelia and Mia having problem with the Victoria Line?

indicators.note: To recollect is to gather things up again, and things gathered up in a hurry seldom go back in the order they were in.

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
ten more letters of fodder, run together as they stand

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Victoria Line' is not the Underground. The disorder ran down Queen Victoria's descendants into the royal families of Russia, Spain and Prussia.
explanation.definitionFit: problem with the Victoria Line -> HAEMOPHILIA: Queen Victoria carried the bleeding disorder and passed it along her line into half the royal houses of Europe.
